attribution.note: Zitron's own judgment in his own post. He quotes Newton only as the setup.

semantics.note: Correctly limited to the one Fediverse report he examined. It is an evaluative observation about how good that report's sources are.

contract.note: The plain reading treats 'flimsy at best' as a verdict on the citation base as a whole, not on every single citation. That is the ordinary reading of the hyperbole. The result rests on one expert audit, because the report itself could not be reached.

evidence.note: Independent audit of the same report, dated before the evaluation date. It finds weak sourcing, including one Reddit post cited six times.
The same audit calls the Twipe article the report's main source, rates it mediocre and finds factual errors in it. This matches the support condition.
Shows that some primary sources, such as Medium's blog post, were cited correctly. This only cuts against a literal every-citation reading, not the overall verdict.

reviews.rationale: The independent audit finds that the report's main and most-repeated sources were a mediocre, error-prone vendor article and a Reddit post. That meets the support condition. The correct Medium citation does not show that the citation base was mostly authoritative. The finding rests on one expert's audit.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: A universal historical claim about year-on-year burn for both companies. It is stated faithfully.

contract.note: Reading 'burn' broadly and covering the years up to 2024 is reasonable. Requiring every year-on-year change to be shown, and leaving missing years unresolved, is fair to an 'every single year' claim.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 filing shows burn and losses rising from 2023 to 2024. It has no figures for 2021 or 2022.
Reported doubling of OpenAI's loss from 2021 to 2022. This confirms one pair of years.
Gives OpenAI's 2024 net loss, but with no 2023 figure the 2022-23 and 2023-24 changes cannot each be confirmed.

reviews.rationale: Increases are confirmed for Anthropic from 2023 to 2024 and for OpenAI from 2021 to 2022. There is no reliable figure for OpenAI in 2023 or for Anthropic in 2021 and 2022. No decrease is documented. Under the contract, missing years leave the claim unresolved.

semantics.note: Keeps his first-person 'I can find no evidence' and his qualifier. In effect it is a hyperbolic, untestable observation.

contract.note: 'Real money' has no threshold, and he dismisses billions in revenue as not real. 'Anyone' is undefined. There is no ordinary test, so not adjudicable is the fair call.

evidence.note: OpenAI had billions in revenue and larger losses. Whether that counts as 'real money' depends on a bar he did not set.

reviews.rationale: The claim reports his own search and turns on an undefined 'real money' standard for unspecified apps and beneficiaries. Revenue figures cannot settle it either way without stretching his words.

attribution.note: Zitron's own statement in his own post.

semantics.note: 'None of these companies are profitable' is a firm claim. 'Doesn't appear to be helping' is a hedged impression and is kept as hedged.

contract.note: Reading 'these companies' as OpenAI and Anthropic in 2024 is fair. Testing the hedged clause by absolute losses matches his own framing of absolute burn. A ratio test (e4) could read differently, so the choice of test matters for that clause.

evidence.note: OpenAI's 2024 net loss was just over $5 billion, so it was not profitable.
Anthropic's net loss in 2024 was $8.31 billion, up from $1.53 billion in 2023, so it was not profitable.
Anthropic's operating loss grew sharply from 2023 to 2024, so absolute losses did not improve.
Compute cost as a share of revenue fell. That is a different metric from the contract's profitability and absolute-loss test, so it counts as context only.

reviews.rationale: Both companies lost money in 2024, and their absolute losses grew, so the firm part holds. The hedged clause matches the absolute-loss test, which is his own frame. Anthropic's compute-to-revenue ratio improved, but that is a different metric, so it is context only.
